messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

the D750 body for Mara Ellison came to our bench on March 6, after she reported that the viewfinder stayed normal but some pictures were black, and that the shutter sometimes sounded slower than what she had selected. Her intake note says this happened first during an indoor school concert, then again outside the following weekend. She did not report a drop or liquid exposure, and there is no mark on the case that points to either one. The body arrived without a lens, battery charger, or memory card. We used a shop battery and a test card for the inspection, so the camera's own card and accessories were not part of the checks. The estimate is being prepared before any repair work, as requested on the intake form.

We recorded the body as a Nikon D750, serial number ending 4821, with 82,416 shutter actuations shown in the menu. The rear screen has a shallow scratch near its lower edge, but it does not cross the displayed image. The rubber around the grip is lifting at the top corner by a few millimeters, and the mode dial turns with its usual resistance. Those details were added to the condition record and are not included as repair items. We did not find a loose screw or a rattling part while moving the body gently. The battery door closes and latches, and the tripod socket has no visible damage.

Initial checks confirmed that the reported problem could be repeated, though it did not happen on every exposure. At 1/250 second, the first set produced two nearly black frames out of twenty. At 1/60 second, one frame in twenty was darker than the others, with an uneven band across the lower third. The stored images on our test card show the same pattern when viewed on the camera and on the bench computer. This makes a card-reading problem less likely, but it does not establish that every black frame in the owner's earlier pictures had the same cause. The viewfinder display stayed on during these checks, and the camera did not show an error message.

After the initial checks we removed the lens mount cover and inspected the shutter curtain area under magnification. The first curtain travels, but the movement is not consistent across the full width; a small hesitation is visible near the right side. We did not see a tear, loose fabric, or a foreign object in the opening. We also checked the mirror return and the aperture actuation using the shop test setup, and those movements appeared consistent in the repeated tests. The work so far has been inspection and diagnosis only. No adjustment or part replacement has been done, and the body was not opened beyond removing the mount cover.

1. The estimate for replacing the shutter assembly is $186 for the part and $210 for labor, making $396 before tax. The shutter assembly is the proposed repair for the uneven curtain travel and inconsistent exposures observed during our checks. Labor includes removing the top and rear covers, transferring the release components to the replacement assembly, fitting it, and checking the travel at several shutter speeds. It also includes reassembling the body and running the final exposure sequence described in the work record. This price is for the body only, with no lens service or other parts included. The estimate does not include work on the screen scratch or grip rubber, which were recorded as condition details rather than reported faults.

The sensor has visible dust, mainly as several small spots in the upper-left area of test images made against an evenly lit surface. We can clean the sensor during the same visit for an additional $45, if Mara wants that added. Sensor cleaning is optional and is not required for the shutter repair. The test frames with the dust spots were made at f/16 against a plain light target; the spots were not apparent in the indoor exposure tests at wider apertures. The $45 figure is separate from the $396 shutter estimate, so the total would be $441 before tax if both jobs are authorized. We have not added the cleaning to the work order, and the estimate currently lists it separately.

The shutter part is not on our shelf today. Our supplier's listing shows stock at its regional warehouse, but that stock has not been confirmed against a purchase order. We would place the order only after receiving authorization for the shutter work. If the supplier confirms the part and it reaches us without a shipping delay, the repair is expected to take seven to ten business days from the time the part arrives here. That is a working estimate rather than a promised completion date. If the supplier cannot provide the listed assembly, we would contact Mara before substituting a different part or changing the quoted amount. No replacement has been ordered at this stage.

The quoted labor assumes that the shutter assembly can be replaced without finding additional damage inside the body. The inspection did not include a full disassembly, and it cannot rule out a second fault that becomes visible only after the covers are removed. If that happens, we would stop before doing additional chargeable work and send a revised estimate for approval. The quoted $396 would not automatically authorize any extra repair. If the shutter assembly is replaced but the black-frame problem remains, the repair record would be updated with the results of the final tests, and any further work would require a separate estimate. We cannot tell from the present checks whether the customer's earlier images were all caused by the shutter, since those original files were not supplied.

The estimate remains open for 30 days from March 6. Prices are before tax, and tax will be calculated on the final invoice according to the shop's billing location. The shop has not received a repair authorization or payment for parts. Mara asked to receive the estimate by email and to be contacted before any repair beyond the inspection, so no approval is recorded on the job ticket. The original inspection notes and the test images are attached to the ticket and can be reviewed with the estimate if she asks. If she declines the repair, the body can be returned in its present assembled condition; the mount cover has already been replaced, and no internal components were removed.

The camera is being kept in a padded cabinet in the service area, separate from bodies waiting for parts. Its battery has been removed since testing, and the test card remains with the inspection materials rather than inside the camera. The current file contains the two test sequences, a photograph of the lifting grip edge, and the screen-condition entry. The viewfinder was not adjusted during inspection, and the stored menu count remains 82,416 in the record.
